why: Most evidence holds. The README FAIL rests on a real gap: index.js exports slugify and README.md has no section for it. It also names a concrete wrong build: add only a padLeft section, so the list stays incomplete. Each PASS names a wrong build and the clause that catches it (for example, "unchanged" catches truncating a longer s). The output fails because the npm test PASS cites the script as "node --test test/", but package.json has "test": "node --test". The criterion requires cited scripts to be real, and this one is misquoted. Line 1 also says "on Node v22.23.4 require(\"./index.js\") loads it". No Node version appears in the repository, so that claim is unsupported. Because cited material is inaccurate, the criterion does not hold for the whole output.
